capabilities.summary: The user-visible Creative Look behavior is documented, but its internal firmware implementation was not located.

evidence.claim: Sony documents ten named Creative Look presets, six Custom Look slots, and adjustable contrast, highlights, shadows, fade, saturation, sharpness, sharpness range, and clarity on ILCE-6700.
Sony documents a Creative Look touch-function icon on both the still-image and movie shooting screens of ILCE-6700.
The bounded ILCE-6700 report labels BODYDATA.DAT as opaque-dat and records no hits for the fixed model, version, filename, and updater token allowlist.

Official documentation is sufficient to define the visible Creative Look control surface, but this metadata-only scan does not locate preset tables, image-processing code, or an ILCE-6400 integration point.

capabilities.next_action: Prepare a separate offline design for approximate Creative Look targets based on the documented controls; do not access or modify the camera.

capabilities.summary: Neither an exact nor a close on-camera Creative Look emulation path is demonstrated by the available evidence.

evidence.claim: Sony describes the intended appearance and adjustment ranges of Creative Looks but does not publish numerical color transforms or processing algorithms on this Help Guide page.
The bounded ILCE-6400 updater report records no hits for the fixed model, version, filename, and updater token allowlist.
The bounded ILCE-6700 package report records no hits for the same fixed token allowlist and does not expose raw firmware content.
Package metadata alone cannot validate a visual match or demonstrate a compatible ILCE-6400 image-pipeline hook.

capabilities.next_action: Require a separate color-reference and algorithm-validation design before considering emulation; do not deploy code to the camera.

capabilities.summary: ILCE-6700 menu and shooting-screen touch behavior is documented, but ILCE-6400 compatibility is not established.

evidence.claim: Sony documents separate ILCE-6700 touch enablement for the shooting screen, footer icons, playback screen, and menu screen, plus swipe actions and touch shooting functions.
Sony lists animal Eye AF, RMT-P1BT support, and stability improvements for ILCE-6400 firmware 2.00; this release-note list does not document a touch-menu interface.
The existence of touch menus on ILCE-6700 does not demonstrate reusable UI code, compatible touch-controller behavior, or an ILCE-6400 firmware interface.

capabilities.next_action: Obtain bounded evidence of an ILCE-6400 touch/UI interface in a separate study; do not test UI code on the camera.

capabilities.summary: The official evidence covers flipped touch-icon placement, not a transplantable full portrait-oriented menu UI.

evidence.claim: Sony documents an ILCE-6700 setting that flips left and right touch-function icon positions when the monitor is flipped.
Sony documents touch-function icons on the left and right sides of the ILCE-6700 shooting screen and their show/hide swipe behavior.
These user-facing descriptions and opaque package metadata do not establish full vertical menu rotation or a compatible ILCE-6400 rendering path.

capabilities.next_action: Find an official definition and bounded implementation interface for portrait UI behavior before any separate design; do not access the camera.

capabilities.summary: Package metadata shows a PE certificate table for the ILCE-6400 updater but does not establish camera-side signature enforcement or a bypass.

evidence.claim: The ILCE-6400 Windows updater is parsed as a five-section PE with a nonzero certificate-table offset and size.
The ILCE-6700 BODYDATA.DAT package is labelled opaque-dat and has no PE summary in the bounded report.
A PE certificate-table entry is not proof of the camera's enforcement boundary and does not provide a signature bypass.
The different outer package formats do not support a direct donor-package transplant conclusion.

capabilities.next_action: Any further signed-container research requires a separate offline design and a verified recovery gate; do not attempt a bypass.

capabilities.summary: The study does not establish whether ILCE-6400 hardware can support the requested ILCE-6700 UI and image-processing behavior.

evidence.claim: The Creative Look Help Guide page identifies the documented camera as ILCE-6700.
The Touch Panel Settings Help Guide page identifies the documented camera as ILCE-6700.
The ILCE-6400 artifact in this study is a Windows PE updater container.
The ILCE-6700 artifact in this study is an opaque DAT container.
These sources do not determine touch-controller, display-orientation, memory, image-processor, or firmware-ABI compatibility between the two camera models.

capabilities.next_action: Require manufacturer architecture documentation or other non-invasive hardware evidence before revisiting compatibility; do not probe the camera.

capabilities.summary: Camera-side experimentation is blocked because this study has no verified ILCE-6400 restore path for a failed modified firmware.

evidence.claim: Sony warns that sudden power loss during the ILCE-6400 update may make the camera inoperable and documents only the official updater workflow on this page.
Sony warns not to remove power during the ILCE-6700 update and documents that non-applicable system software is rejected for the target model.
The bounded ILCE-6400 report contains package format, PE metadata, entropy windows, and allowlisted token hits; it does not demonstrate a restore operation.

Without an independently verified restore path, the official inoperability warning and the lack of a demonstrated restore interface make camera-side firmware experiments unacceptable under this study's safety gate.

capabilities.next_action: End this study offline; require a separately validated ILCE-6400 recovery method and a nonessential test body before any camera-side proposal.
